chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Thornton Blue, the St. Louis clarinetist who challenged Buster Bailey
summary: Thornton Blue hounded Buster Bailey until Bailey let him play, and he was a virtuoso whose father led the Imperial Band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: There was a great clarinet player named Blue. Do you remember Blue?
Thornton Blue, with the big teeth.
Yeah. Thornton Blue came out of St. Louis in the wake of ...(?)...
...and he asked for Buster. And he hounded Buster for every (?) second(?).

So Buster said finally, "Go get your horn," and they went in the joint and they blew it all night. And Blue was a virtuoso. He'd come out of St. Louis. His father had the Imperial Band. I hung out with him a while. He told me a lot...
